part: Treasure Chess sky panoramas: academic Whitby companions
note: Open-sea companions for the academic-realist Whitby paintings, to complete the 360-degree sky. Claude, 25 Nov 2026.
style: One single wide, highly finished academic-realist oil painting, nineteenth-century salon quality: precise drawing, smooth glazed paint, true atmosphere. No town, no abbey, no church, no lighthouse, no ships, no boats, no people; no text, lettering, signature, monogram, frame, border or black bars.

beats.text: Open sea under towering golden cumulus and a deep blue sky, late-afternoon light from the right, calm deep-blue water with long gentle swell, in the manner of Edward William Cooke and Ivan Aivazovsky. This picture is the section of one wide panorama that lies immediately to the LEFT of the reference painting, seen from the same spot far out at sea. At the far right edge the coastline continues where the reference painting begins: the same cliffs and rocky shore, small and distant on the horizon, running in from the right edge for about a fifth of the width and then ending, so the rest of the picture is open sea and sky. The horizon is at exactly the same height as in the reference, perfectly level; the same light, the same weather, the same painting.

Open sea at night in a gale, heavy storm clouds lit at their edges by the moon (the moon itself is not in this picture), rough sea with breaking waves and moonlit spray, in the manner of Ivan Aivazovsky.
